thematicCorridors.name: Inga–Kolwezi–Johannesburg Southern HVDC Power Backbone
thematicCorridors.description: High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) corridor interconnecting the Congo River hydro complex through the Zambian Copperbelt into the Southern African Power Pool (SAPP).
thematicCorridors.source: EC JRC Clean Energy Access Tool & SAPP Grid Atlas

thematicCorridors.name: West African Power Pool (WAPP) Coastal Interconnector
thematicCorridors.description: 330 kV transmission spine linking Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Togo, Benin, and Nigeria to create a unified West African electricity market.

thematicCorridors.name: Eastern Africa Power Pool (EAPP) High-Voltage Interconnector
thematicCorridors.description: 500 kV HVDC intertie wheeling renewable hydroelectric power from Ethiopia’s highlands and Lake Turkana wind energy to Kenya and Tanzania.
thematicCorridors.source: EAPP Master Plan / JRC Energy Matrix

thematicCorridors.name: Kavango–Zambezi (KAZA) Transfrontier Wildlife Corridor
thematicCorridors.description: The world’s largest transboundary conservation area encompassing 520,000 km² across Angola, Botswana, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

thematicCorridors.name: Nile Basin Freshwater & Ecological Lifeline
thematicCorridors.description: Vital continental freshwater spine spanning 6,650 km supporting over 300 million people across 11 riparian nations.
thematicCorridors.source: Global Surface Water Explorer / EC JRC

thematicCorridors.name: Guinea Savanna Agricultural Transformation Belt
thematicCorridors.description: A 600-million hectare agricultural frontier with high agro-ecological potential for maize, soybean, cassava, and livestock.
thematicCorridors.source: FAO / EC JRC Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS)

thematicCorridors.name: East African Rift Agricultural & Grain Artery
thematicCorridors.description: High-fertility volcanic rift valley corridor linking Ethiopian teff/coffee highlands to Kenyan and Tanzanian cereal belts.

thematicCorridors.name: Abidjan–Lagos Coastal Megalopolis Corridor
thematicCorridors.description: One of the world’s fastest-growing urban agglomerations, projected to house over 50 million people by 2035 along a continuous 1,000 km coastal belt.

thematicCorridors.name: Gauteng–Durban Industrial & Demographic Belt
thematicCorridors.description: South Africa’s primary industrial artery connecting the 16-million Gauteng urban agglomeration to the continent’s busiest container terminal at Port of Durban.
thematicCorridors.source: GHSL / World Bank Urban Accessibility Index

thematicCorridors.name: Trans-Sahara Multimodal Highway (TAH 2 / Algiers–Lagos)
thematicCorridors.description: Strategic 4,500 km transcontinental trade highway linking the Mediterranean at Algiers through Niger to the Atlantic at Lagos, anchoring the AfCFTA interior trade.
thematicCorridors.source: AU AfCFTA Secretariat & UN ECA Infrastructure Master Plan

thematicCorridors.name: East African Northern Trade Corridor (Mombasa–Nairobi–Kigali)
thematicCorridors.description: The highest-throughput logistics corridor in Eastern and Central Africa, connecting landlocked Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and Eastern DRC to the Port of Mombasa.
thematicCorridors.source: Northern Corridor Transit and Transport Coordination Authority

thematicAuras.name: The Great Green Wall of Africa (Sahelian Restoration Belt)
thematicAuras.description: An 8,000 km natural wonder initiative spanning 11 nations across the width of the continent to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land and sequester 250M tons of carbon.
thematicAuras.source: Pan-African Agency of the Great Green Wall / EC JRC

thematicAuras.name: Congo Basin Primary Rainforest Ecological Shield
thematicAuras.description: The second largest tropical rainforest on Earth and the world’s most effective net carbon sink, absorbing 1.5 billion tons of CO2 annually.
thematicAuras.source: Copernicus Global Land Cover & Global Forest Watch / JRC

thematicPulseNodes.name: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD)
thematicPulseNodes.label: GERD Hydro Complex
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Hydroelectric Super-Project
thematicPulseNodes.description: Africa’s largest hydroelectric facility, doubling Ethiopia’s electricity generation and exporting clean baseload power to Sudan, Djibouti, and Kenya.
thematicPulseNodes.source: EC JRC Global Dam Watch / Ethiopian Electric Power

thematicPulseNodes.name: Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex
thematicPulseNodes.label: Noor Solar CSP
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Concentrated Solar Power
thematicPulseNodes.description: One of the world’s largest concentrated solar power (CSP) installations with utility-scale molten-salt thermal energy storage delivering power through night-time peak hours.

thematicPulseNodes.name: Benban Solar Park
thematicPulseNodes.label: Benban Solar Park
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Photovoltaic Mega-Array
thematicPulseNodes.description: A 37.2 km² solar park in Egypt’s Western Desert, visibly distinct from orbit and supplying clean electricity to over 1 million homes.
thematicPulseNodes.source: New and Renewable Energy Authority (NREA) / AKP

thematicPulseNodes.name: Lake Turkana Wind Power Project
thematicPulseNodes.label: Lake Turkana Wind
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Sub-Saharan Wind Farm
thematicPulseNodes.description: Africa’s largest wind farm, tapping into the hyper-reliable Turkana low-level jet stream to feed the Kenyan national grid.

thematicPulseNodes.name: Serengeti & Ngorongoro Ecosystem
thematicPulseNodes.label: Serengeti Biosphere
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: UNESCO World Heritage
thematicPulseNodes.description: The oldest and most protected grassland ecosystem on Earth, featuring the iconic annual circular migration of over 2 million ungulates.

thematicPulseNodes.name: Okavango Delta Inland Wetland
thematicPulseNodes.label: Okavango Delta
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Ramsar Wetland Site
thematicPulseNodes.description: One of the few interior delta systems without an oceanic outlet, flooding during the dry winter season to create an oasis for African biodiversity.

thematicPulseNodes.name: Lagos Metropolitan Megacity
thematicPulseNodes.label: Lagos Megacity
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Commercial Powerhouse
thematicPulseNodes.description: Sub-Saharan Africa’s largest urban economy and financial nexus, expanding rapidly with Lekki Deep Sea Port and financial free zones.
thematicPulseNodes.source: Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) / UN Habitat

thematicPulseNodes.name: Greater Cairo Metropolitan Area
thematicPulseNodes.label: Greater Cairo
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Continental Megacity
thematicPulseNodes.description: The largest metropolitan area in Africa and the Arab world, pioneering smart urban expansion with the New Administrative Capital.
thematicPulseNodes.source: GHSL / World Bank Urban Development Unit

thematicPulseNodes.name: Gauteng Megalopolis (Johannesburg–Pretoria)
thematicPulseNodes.label: Johannesburg–Pretoria
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Financial & Industrial Hub
thematicPulseNodes.description: Africa’s primary financial capital and corporate command center, anchoring the economic engine of Southern Africa.

thematicPulseNodes.name: Tanger Med Port Complex & Logistics Free Zone
thematicPulseNodes.label: Tanger Med Gateway
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Global Mediterranean Transshipment
thematicPulseNodes.description: The leading container port on the African continent and in the Mediterranean basin, directly connecting 180 global ports across 70 countries.
thematicPulseNodes.source: Tanger Med Port Authority / UNCTAD Maritime Review

thematicPulseNodes.name: Port of Durban Multimodal Trade Gateway
thematicPulseNodes.label: Port of Durban
thematicPulseNodes.subtitle: Southern African Sea Hub
thematicPulseNodes.description: The primary maritime trade gate for South Africa and landlocked neighbors including Botswana, Zimbabwe, and Zambia.
thematicPulseNodes.source: Transnet National Ports Authority / AfCFTA Trade Map
